rag_summary_count_consistency.details: The RAG output reports no identified biases and provides zero identified occurrences. Its single candidate is separately represented in candidate_biases.

evaluation_limitations: No retrieved corpus passages or retrieval logs were supplied, so corpus fidelity cannot be scored.
The supplied segment map has no hidden bias instances; instance-level recall and occurrence-match rates therefore have undefined denominators.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: Mainly to see whether adopting something pre-built could shortcut months of remediation work, given the timeline.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant states a time-constrained evaluation goal without a manifested cognitive-bias instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: Rather than take that at face value, I asked for their contrast-ratio spec sheet... it only covered default, unthemed values... our actual implementation would always be themed.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant seeks direct evidence and identifies the limits of the available spec before deciding scope.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: I scoped the pilot narrowly — just the token categories tied directly to our compliance gap... since the spec sheet could not tell me how the tokens would hold up once themed.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The narrow pilot is explicitly tied to an evidence gap and the compliance need.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: The demo was impressive, but impressive motion design on one component does not tell you much about contrast behavior on a different set of tokens, so I kept those separate in my head.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant explicitly separates component-level motion evidence from token contrast evidence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: I mapped what the narrow pilot actually needed against each tier’s component list... Team actually covered our confirmed needs... I recommended Team.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The tier choice is based on confirmed component requirements and comparison against each tier.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: I asked both squad leads directly what their earliest realistic integration window was... One could start in three weeks, the other in five. I set the rollout date to the later window.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The date is set from both squads’ stated feasible windows rather than an unsupported internal assumption.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: Checking actual needs against the tier list and getting real calendar commitments from both squads is basically what I would do again.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant restates an evidence-based decision process; no bias instance is intended or manifested.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: I had told the VP and both squad leads earlier that the defaults tested well... but I had also flagged at the time that full-scale testing was still pending.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant reports both the preliminary result and its pending-testing caveat.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: I wanted to know whether the failure was in our theming layer or in the vendor’s own default tokens, so I requested an independent retest... I did not want to guess at the cause.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The retest is a diagnostic step to distinguish competing causal explanations.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: Once the retest pointed at the vendor defaults specifically, I reverted just the three affected components... and left the rest... in place, since those had tested clean.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant takes a selective action keyed to retest evidence and component-level test results.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: The hybrid matched what the evidence actually showed — keep what tested clean, source internally what did not... I documented the retest findings, expected migration effort, and compliance risk for each option.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The final recommendation compares alternatives using test evidence, migration effort, and compliance risk.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: I would keep asking for direct evidence... The one thing I would tighten up is flagging the pending full-scale testing caveat more visibly in written updates.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant identifies a communication improvement while retaining evidence-seeking practices.

rag_label_false_positive_inventory.mechanism_overlap_summary: The candidate describes a plausible social-proof mechanism, but the hidden manifest contains no target bias instance.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: The RAG achieved zero false alarms across all identified-confidence thresholds, with 12 correct rejections. Including candidates produced one false alarm among 12 negative segments.
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: No hidden bias instances were present, so strict instance-level precision, recall, and F1 are undefined without candidates and equal zero precision and F1 with the candidate included.
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: Mechanism-first results are identical to strict results because the candidate does not correspond to a hidden bias instance.
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: The candidate was a useful abstention: it was quote-grounded, plausible, and explicitly withheld as an identified bias due to insufficient evidence.
main_failure_modes: Counting the useful candidate as a detection at the candidate-inclusive threshold creates one false alarm on a negative segment.
main_strengths: No unsupported identified bias occurrences were produced.
The candidate included valid localization and a clear explanation of why it was not promoted.
The RAG correctly recognized the absence of retrieved corpus support.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This is a strong zero-bias-control result for identified findings, with a small expected false-alarm tradeoff when plausible candidates are included.
